about: Every catch (\Throwable) under lib/Service that answers null or [] within its first three statements. ServiceCatchReturnsNullTest fails on a site that is not here, on an entry whose site is gone, and when the count passes the ceiling. The ceiling only goes down.

This is a debt list with a ceiling, not an endorsement. The class and the reason on each entry were written by the triage that seeded this file on 2026-09-13 from the site's own evidence: what it returns, and whether and how it logs. They say what the site does, not that the site is right.

The refusal class is deliberately absent: a site where a rule said no is converted to a RefusedException and leaves this file (REQ-QG-CRN-2). Four left it on 2026-09-13, all four in the guard-resolver class hydra gate 8 exists for. Any entry below may turn out to be a refusal when someone reads it; that is what the next batch is for.

The proposal measured 47 sites over a three-LINE window. This instrument counts three STATEMENTS, because a multi-line logger call in front of the return is the same shape and a line window cannot see it. The same tree reads 90 by lines and 203 by statements.

Merging development on 2026-09-14 brought new sites with it, and moved one. #2719 added `Substitution/HumaniqLeaveReader::readLeave#1`. #2732 split `Flow/CaseFlowActions` and added `Flow/PlannedSeriesLedger::optional#1`, `::plannedFlows#1` and `::rowsOf#1`, which is also where `CaseFlowActions::plannedFlows` went, so that entry is removed here rather than kept. The ceiling went 203 to 206 for those four sites and nothing else.

2026-09-14, openspec/changes/one-date-write-path: three nulling date parsers left lib/ (CaseEnricher::normaliseDate, TermijnTimerService::dateOrNull, WorkQueueService::parseDateOnly) and three CaseDateNormaliser sites arrived, two zone-resolution degradations and one read-path reader. The ceiling is unchanged at 206; every write path refuses now instead of answering null.

2026-09-14, openspec/changes/inbound-mail-filters: nine sites arrived with the mail intake path. Eight are degradations of an OPTIONAL app, Nextcloud Mail, which is absent on most instances and whose service, account, attachment, folder and event readers each log at warning and answer the documented empty value; the ninth is the read-miss on an intake log entry. The ceiling went 206 to 215 for those nine and nothing else.

2026-09-14, openspec/changes/case-grants-name-their-source: four sites arrived with OpenRegisterGrantsGateway, the one place dossiq asks OpenRegister who may do what on a case. All four are degradations of an app that may be absent or may predate openregister#3726, and each logs at warning naming what was absent. The null is load-bearing rather than tolerated: the caller reads null as "carry on" and false as "OpenRegister refused", and collapsing the two would lock every handler out of every case on an instance that has not upgraded. The ceiling went 215 to 219 for those four and nothing else.

classes.refusal: A rule said no. Throw a typed exception and let the controller translate it (ADR-105). Never allowlisted: converting it is the fix.
classes.degradation: A sibling app, an engine or a container binding is absent. Keep the catch, log at warning naming what was absent, return the documented empty value.
classes.read-miss: An object was not found on a read. Answering null is right; the catch is how the store reports the miss.

sites.reason: `provenanceForCase()` answers `return null` when OpenRegister's evaluator throws; the catch logs at warning naming the case ("OpenRegister could not answer the provenance for a case") and the caller publishes the action list exactly as it would without OpenRegister. Null is deliberately NOT false here: reading "we could not ask" as "refused" would empty every case's action list on every instance that has not upgraded to openregister#3726.
